'''Tom Sanders''' {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} is an English mathematician, working on problems in [[additive combinatorics]] at the interface of [[harmonic analysis]] and [[analytic number theory]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/~sanders/|title=Tom Sanders Homepage in Oxford|website=people.maths.ox.ac.uk}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://arxiv.org/a/sanders_t_1 |title=Tom Sanders's articles on arXiv |website=Arxiv.org |date= |accessdate=9 March 2017}}</ref>

==Education==
Sanders studied mathematics at the [[University of Cambridge]], where he was awarded a PhD in 2007 for research on [[arithmetic combinatorics]] supervised by  [[Timothy Gowers]].<ref name=mathgene/><ref name=phd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Cambridge|title=Topics in arithmetic combinatorics|first= Tom|last=Sanders|date=2007|url=https://www.repository.cam.ac.uk/handle/1810/236994|website=cam.ac.uk|oclc=879379453}} {{open access}}</ref> 

==Career and research==
He held a Junior [[Research Fellow]]ship at [[Christ's College, Cambridge]] from 2006 until 2011, in addition to visiting fellowships at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in 2007, the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|MSRI]] in 2008, and the [[Mittag-Leffler Institute]] in 2009. Since 2011, he has held a [[Royal Society University Research Fellowship]] (URF)<ref name=urfrs/> at the [[University of Oxford]], where he is also a senior research fellow at the [[Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford|Mathematical Institute]], and a Tutorial Fellow at [[St Hugh's College, Oxford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/people/tom.sanders|title=Tom Sanders, Mathematical Institute|website=maths.ox.ac.uk}}</ref> 

Among other results, he has improved the theorem of [[Klaus Friedrich Roth]] on three-term [[arithmetic progression]]s,<ref>{{cite journal|authorlink=Klaus Friedrich Roth|first=Klaus Friedrich|last=Roth|title=On certain sets of integers|journal=[[Journal of the London Mathematical Society]]|volume=28|pages=104–109|year=1953|zbl=0050.04002|mr=0051853|doi=10.1112/jlms/s1-28.1.104}}</ref> coming close to breaking the so-called logarithmic barrier. More precisely, he has shown that any subset of {1, 2, ..., ''N''} of maximal cardinality containing no non-trivial three-term arithmetic progression is of size <math>O\!\left(\frac{N (\log \log N)^5}{\log N}\right)\;\!\!\!.</math><ref>{{cite journal| authorlink=Tom Sanders (mathematician)|first=Tom|last=Sanders | title=On Roth's theorem on progressions | journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]|volume=174|issue=1|year=2011|pages=619–636|mr=2811612 | doi=10.4007/annals.2011.174.1.20 | arxiv=1011.0104|s2cid=53331882 }}</ref>

===Awards and honours===
In February 2011, he was awarded the [[Adams Prize]] (jointly with [[Harald Helfgott]]) for having "employed deep harmonic analysis to understand arithmetic progressions and answer long-standing conjectures in [[number theory]]".<ref>{{cite journal| title=Helfgott and Sanders Awarded Adams Prize | journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=58|issue=7|page=966| url=http://www.ams.org/notices/201107/rtx110700966p.pdf | year=2011}} (Reprinted from a University of Cambridge announcement.)</ref> In July 2012, he was awarded a Prize of the [[European Mathematical Society]] for his "fundamental results in additive combinatorics and harmonic analysis, which combine in a masterful way deep known techniques with the invention of new methods to achieve spectacular results."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.6ecm.pl/en | title=6th European Congress of Mathematics |website=6ecm.pl |date= |accessdate=9 March 2017}}</ref> In July 2013, he was awarded the [[Whitehead Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/lms-prizes-2013 |title=LMS Prizes 2014 | publisher=[[London Mathematical Society]] | location=UK |website=Lms.ac.uk |date=9 July 2013 |accessdate=9 March 2017}}</ref> for his "spectacular results in additive combinatorics and related areas"'', ''in particular "for his paper obtaining the best known upper bounds for sets of integers containing no 3-term arithmetic progressions, for his work dramatically improving bounds connected with [[Freiman's theorem]] on sets with small doubling, and for other results in additive combinatorics and harmonic analysis."<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/node/837 | publisher=[[University of Oxford Mathematical Institute]] | location=UK | title=Nick Trefethen, Frances Kirwan, Fernando Alday and Tom Sanders awarded LMS prizes for 2013 | date=29 September 2014 | accessdate=3 June 2020}}</ref> In September 2013, he was awarded the [[European Prize in Combinatorics]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/node/869 | publisher=[[University of Oxford Mathematical Institute]] | location=UK | title=Tom Sanders wins the European Prize in Combinatorics | date=29 September 2014 | accessdate=3 June 2020}}</ref>
